p.hi: Paper Prepared by the Deputy Special Representative for Trade Negotiations (Pearce)

div.p: 1. Delay House action on the trade bill until it is clear that Title IV issues can be resolved to our satisfaction (i.e., by defeating the Vanik amendment or dropping Title IV).

list.label: a.
list.item: Avoids unfavorable House action on MFN, credit while Middle East issues unresolved (though see Con #e).
list.label: b.
list.item: Avoids threat of veto which would undermine prospects for the bill.
list.label: c.
list.item: Provides time in which to turn the House around on the Title IV issue.
list.label: d.
list.item: No real evidence the EC is prepared to go forward now anyway.

list.label: a.
list.item: Delay increases risk that opponents of TRA will gain strength—we now have votes to pass it.
list.label: b.
list.item: Doubtful that Title IV issues can be resolved before the House recesses. Pushing House action into next year jeopardizes momentum in trade negotiations. Enables France, others to pull back, blame U.S.
list.label: c.
list.item: Reflects choice between Soviet détente and relationships with major allies, obligations to LDC’s.
list.label: d.
list.item: Increases hostility of W&M members who comprise our most solid House support for the TRA.
list.label: e.
list.item: Vanik amendment could be added to another bill (possibly veto-proof). If so, we would lose both ends.

div.p: 2. Proceed on the basis of Mr. Ullman’s proposal (a privileged W&M committee amendment to drop Title IV).

list.label: a.
list.item: Would commit W&M to support dropping Title IV.
list.label: b.
list.item: If succeeds, strengthens somewhat prospects for beating Vanik amendment (since committee amendment precedes Vanik amendment).
list.label: c.
list.item: Avoids further delay in House vote, thus reduces chances of AFL–CIO chipping away necessary sup-port.

list.label: a.
list.item: Forces issue in House before Jewish counter effort has time to succeed.
list.label: b.
list.item: Forfeits W&M responsibility for passage of the bill. (Ullman has said he will support a committee amendment if the President asks, but then the President bears the responsibility if bill fails.)
list.label: c.
list.item: Effect of success in dropping Title IV on vote hard to appraise—could result in defeat in House. All of our vote counts are based on the assumption that Title IV (and, presumably Vanik) are in the bill. This means liberal Democrats with obligations to Meany can vote for him on Title IV, then against him on bill. If they are pressured to vote against him on Title IV, it is hard to predict their votes on the bill.
list.label: d.
list.item: Doubtful we will have effective support of the liberal trade community. (This could change if solid evidence of support in the Jewish community emerges.)
list.label: e.
list.item: If succeed, still must contend with Jackson forces in Senate.
list.label: f.
list.item: No assurance that we can avoid or defeat the Vanik credit amendment even if we prevail on the committee amendment. Could end up with no MFN authority, restrictions on credit in House bill.

div.p: 3. Proceed with action in the House. Seek deletion of Title IV but without asking for a committee amendment. Then work toward a solution in the Senate.

list.label: a.
list.item: Bill will pass (albeit with Vanik amendment, Title IV). Have basis for trade bill we want in conference where House usually wins on trade issues.
list.label: b.
list.item: Sets stage for a better considered, executed effort in Senate. More time for Jewish community to work for compromise. In the end, we must deal with Jackson anyway.
list.label: c.
list.item: Avoids delay in preparations, loss of momentum in negotiations. d. Avoids for now a Presidential “choice” between détente with Soviets and accommodation of allies, LDC’s.
list.label: e.
list.item: Soviet reaction could be moderated somewhat by effective diplomatic effort pointing out we have other chance to come out where we want to be by dealing with the issues in the Senate where there are fewer “cold warriors.”

list.label: a.
list.item: Risks offense to Soviets in critical Middle East period.
list.label: b.
list.item: Could increase difficulty in negotiating with Jackson since he has what he wants in the House bill.
